paragraphs.title: Ziba Offers Assistance and David Punishes Mephibosheth

easy.explanation: Ziba, the servant of Mephibosheth, met David.
easy.q: Who met David just after he passed the top of the hill?

easy.explanation: Ziba brought saddled donkeys, bread, raisins, summer fruits, and wine.
easy.q: What did Ziba bring for David and his men?

easy.explanation: Ziba said that Mephibosheth abode at Jerusalem.
easy.q: Where did Ziba say Mephibosheth was staying?

answers: Because he hoped to regain his father's kingdom
To help David in the wilderness
medium.explanation: Ziba claimed that Mephibosheth expected the house of Israel to restore his father's kingdom.
medium.q: Why did Ziba say Mephibosheth had remained at Jerusalem?

answers: The king's household to ride on
medium.explanation: Ziba said, “The asses be for the king’s household to ride on.”
medium.q: Who were the donkeys intended for?

answers: He gave Ziba everything belonging to Mephibosheth
He ordered Ziba to return the food
medium.explanation: David said, “Behold, thine are all that pertained unto Mephibosheth.”
medium.q: What did David do after hearing Ziba's report?

answers: Ziba appears to assist David, while Mephibosheth is portrayed as seeking the kingdom
Ziba rebels against David, while Mephibosheth helps him
challenge.explanation: Ziba presents himself as helpful and Mephibosheth as someone hoping to gain the throne.
challenge.q: What contrast does Ziba present between himself and Mephibosheth?

answers: David accepted the claim and acted on it
David asked Absalom to investigate it
challenge.explanation: David gave Ziba Mephibosheth's property after hearing the accusation.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David's immediate response to Ziba?

answers: He and his men needed food, transportation, and drink
They were living comfortably in the palace
They were preparing a feast for Absalom
challenge.explanation: The supplies Ziba brought were useful to people traveling under difficult conditions.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes David's condition while fleeing?

paragraphs.title: Shimei Curses David and David Accepts the Affliction

easy.explanation: Shimei the son of Gera came out and cursed David.
easy.q: Who cursed David and threw stones at him?

easy.explanation: Abishai asked permission to go over and take off Shimei's head.
easy.q: What did Abishai want to do to Shimei?

answers: They rested because they were weary
easy.explanation: The king and the people came weary and refreshed themselves there.
easy.q: What did David and his people do at the end of the passage?

answers: David thought the LORD might have told Shimei to curse him
medium.explanation: David considered that the LORD might have appointed Shimei's cursing as part of his affliction.
medium.q: Why did David not allow Abishai to take revenge on Shimei?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes David and his people resting after becoming weary.
medium.q: In the context of the passage, what does “refreshed themselves” mean?

answers: That the LORD would repay him with good
That Absalom would immediately return to him
medium.explanation: David said, “It may be that the LORD will look on mine affliction, and ... requite me good.”
medium.q: What hope did David express after Shimei's curse?

answers: He sees it as possibly connected with God's chastening and does not rush to retaliate
He ignores it and continues celebrating
He says it has no meaning at all
challenge.explanation: David accepts that the LORD may have allowed the affliction and restrains revenge.
challenge.q: What attitude toward suffering is shown by David's words?

answers: The cursing happened only once and ended quickly
Shimei continued troubling David along the way
challenge.explanation: Shimei continued cursing, throwing stones, and casting dust as he went.
challenge.q: What does the description of Shimei walking opposite David emphasize?

answers: Because David was fleeing after Absalom's rebellion, he faced Shimei's abuse without taking revenge
Because David rested, Shimei stopped cursing
Because Shimei cursed, David immediately entered Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: David's troubled condition during the flight influenced his decision not to retaliate.
challenge.q: What cause-and-effect relationship appears between David's flight and his response?

easy.explanation: Absalom and all the people with him came to Jerusalem.
easy.q: Who came to Jerusalem with all the people of Israel?

easy.explanation: Hushai is identified as David's friend.
easy.q: Who was Hushai according to the passage?

easy.explanation: Hushai said, “God save the king, God save the king.”
easy.q: What did Hushai say to Absalom?

answers: Hushai was David's friend and had not gone with David
Hushai had not arrived at Jerusalem
Hushai was one of Shimei's men
medium.explanation: Absalom asked why Hushai had not gone with his friend David.
medium.q: Why was Absalom surprised that Hushai had come to him?

answers: He said he should serve the king chosen by the LORD and the king's son
He said he wanted Mephibosheth's property
He said he had come only to rest
medium.explanation: Hushai said he would serve the one chosen by the LORD and the people, as well as the king's son.
medium.q: How did Hushai explain remaining with Absalom?

answers: I will fight against all Israel
medium.explanation: Hushai declares that he will stay with the king whom he claims to support.
medium.q: What does the phrase “with him will I abide” mean in context?

answers: He presents his loyalty to Absalom in respectful and persuasive language
He brings Absalom a large supply of food
He reveals all of David's plans
challenge.explanation: Hushai claims that he should serve the king and his son, so Absalom accepts him.
challenge.q: What allows Hushai to gain access to Absalom?

answers: He is David's friend, but he presents himself as Absalom's servant
He is Absalom's son, but presents himself as a stranger
He is Shimei's man, but presents himself as king
challenge.explanation: The passage identifies Hushai as David's friend, although he speaks as if he supports Absalom.
challenge.q: What tension exists between Hushai's identity and his words?

answers: He says he will serve the one chosen by the LORD, the people, and Israel's men
He says only Mephibosheth was chosen
He says there is no chosen king
challenge.explanation: Hushai refers to the choice of the LORD and the people to explain his apparent loyalty.
challenge.q: How does Hushai use the idea of choosing to justify his position?

paragraphs.title: Ahithophel's Counsel and the Act Concerning David's Concubines

easy.explanation: Absalom asked Ahithophel what they should do.
easy.q: Whom did Absalom ask for counsel?

answers: Go in unto his father's concubines
easy.explanation: Ahithophel advised Absalom to go in unto David's concubines.
easy.q: What did Ahithophel advise Absalom to do?

answers: Upon the top of the house
easy.explanation: A tent was spread for Absalom upon the top of the house.
easy.q: Where was the tent spread for the act?

answers: All Israel would hear that Absalom was hated by his father, and his supporters would be strengthened
David would be able to rest in the wilderness
medium.explanation: Ahithophel connected public knowledge of the act with strengthening Absalom's supporters.
medium.q: According to Ahithophel, what was the purpose of his counsel?

medium.explanation: Ahithophel meant that the act would make Absalom openly hated by David.
medium.q: In the phrase “thou art abhorred of thy father,” what does “abhorred” mean?

answers: A tent was spread on the roof, and Absalom went in unto the concubines
medium.explanation: The passage says the tent was set up and Absalom carried out the counsel publicly.
medium.q: What happened after Ahithophel gave his counsel?

answers: So all Israel would hear of it and Absalom's supporters would be strengthened
So the change of kingship could remain secret
challenge.explanation: Ahithophel said that all Israel should hear about the act and that Absalom's supporters would then be strengthened.
challenge.q: Why was the act involving David's concubines made public according to Ahithophel?

answers: It was regarded as though someone had inquired at the oracle of God
challenge.explanation: His counsel was considered exceptionally authoritative by both David and Absalom.
challenge.q: What does the closing statement reveal about Ahithophel's counsel?

answers: It publicly displayed Absalom's irreversible break with David and strengthened the rebellion
challenge.explanation: The public act demonstrated the rupture with David and reinforced Absalom's claim to rule.
challenge.q: How did the counsel support the transfer of kingship?
